table_description: Organizational structure for the SAMPLE schema. One row per department with its name, the employee number of the department manager, the parent (administering) department, and the physical location. Departments form a tree via the self-referential ADMRDEPT column.
use_cases: Resolve a department number ('A00', 'D11') to a human-readable name
Walk the department hierarchy via ADMRDEPT (each department's parent)
Find the manager of a given department by joining MGRNO back to EMPLOYEE.EMPNO
Identify departments without a manager (MGRNO IS NULL)
Count employees per department by joining to EMPLOYEE.WORKDEPT
data_quality_notes: DEPTNO is CHAR(3) and the primary key — compare with string literals ('A00'), not integers.
MGRNO is CHAR(6) matching EMPLOYEE.EMPNO; it is nullable — not every department has a manager assigned.
ADMRDEPT is self-referential: a department's parent is another department's DEPTNO. The root departments point at themselves.
LOCATION is often NULL or blank in the shipped data; don't rely on it as a required field.
Names in DEPTNAME use mixed-case English; case-insensitive comparison (UPPER()) is safer for free-form search.

table_columns.name: MGRNO
table_columns.description: Employee number of the department manager. Foreign key to EMPLOYEE.EMPNO.

table_columns.name: ADMRDEPT
table_columns.description: Administering (parent) department. Self-referential foreign key to DEPARTMENT.DEPTNO — root departments point at themselves.

table_columns.name: LOCATION
table_columns.description: Physical location of the department (often blank in the shipped sample data).
